title: Publishing compact playbook for beta partners
content:
Purpose and scope:
A short, pragmatic playbook for getting a small set of strategic beta partners onto the cloud catalog quickly (2–4 week runway). Focused on: minimal acceptance gates, tile & trial copy variants, billing SKU alignment, and a lightweight risk matrix for legal/compliance. This is intentionally compact — meant to be used in parallel with partner onboarding calls and engineering readiness checks.

Target audience:
- GTM PM / Partner Manager owning the partner relationship
- Partner engineering contact (integration lead)
- Marketplace ops / listing owner (Redwood)
- Legal/compliance punt: commercial counsel for final sign-off

High-level goals (beta):
- Get partner tile live in a single region with a controlled trial experience
- Validate conversion funnel (trial -> paid) within partner cohort
- Surface early integration issues (auth, routing, SKU) and measure latency/cost signal

Quick timeline (recommended):
Week 0: kickoff + tile copy + legal checklist sent
Week 1: engineering smoke tests + billing SKU alignment
Week 2: private listing + partner verification (QA session)
Week 3: soft live (invite-only) + monitoring window
Week 4: review metrics, iterate copy, plan broader publish

Minimum acceptance gates (go/no-go):
1) Tile approval: Microcopy verified by partner and Redwood brand (tile title, 2-line blurb, one CTA).
2) Billing SKU mapping: Partner SKU mapped to Redwood pricing matrix OR documented pass-through model.
3) Auth path validated: partner can create and revoke API keys; token exchange documented and smoke-tested.
4) Trial controls: trial credit mechanics work (expiration, redemption, entitlement) in sandbox.
5) Security snapshot: partner attests to data handling and agrees to minimal logging/PII rules (one-pager).
6) Rollback plan: clearly documented rollback trigger and contact list.

Tile & microcopy variants (pick 2 to A/B during beta):
- Variant A (concise): "SmartSummarize — Enterprise-quality summarization, low-latency. Try free credits."
- Variant B (persona-led): "SmartSummarize for Customer Success — Fast, accurate recaps from support transcripts. Get started with free credits."
- Variant C (feature-first): "Summarize long docs into bullets, preserve actions. 50 free credits on sign-up."

CTA recommendations:
- Primary: "Start free trial" (opens private trial flow)
- Secondary: "See integration guide" (links to quickstart docs)

Trial flow (minimal):
1) Partner issues invite link (unique token) to customer
2) Customer redeems trial on Redwood Console (auto-provision trial credits)
3) Trial telemetry auto-tagged with partner-id for cohort analysis
4) Trial expiration triggers grace email; optional conversion CTA

Required assets checklist (shiplist):
- 1x 160x160 tile icon (png, transparent)
- 1x 16:9 hero image (for detail page)
- Tile title (<= 60 chars)
- 2-line blurb (<= 150 chars)
- Short integration quickstart (Markdown) with auth examples
- Billing SKU mapping doc (spreadsheet row)

Risk matrix (quick):
- Legal/compliance: medium — partner must sign the data-addendum; if not, block live.
- Latency/Perf: low-medium — run 100 sample requests, flag >2s p50 for ops review.
- Billing mismatch: medium-high — if SKU cannot map to our pricing tiers, escalate pricing ops.
- Misleading claims: high — any claim on model capability that conflicts with Redwood marketing policy = block.

Operational playbook (engineer checklist):
- [ ] Add partner to staging allowlist
- [ ] Add partner-id tag in telemetry pipeline
- [ ] Configure trial-credit redemption rule (limit one per customer-email)
- [ ] Validate region routing and fallback model variant
- [ ] Configure quota & rate-limit for partner cohort

Metrics to monitor first 7 days (dashboard quick list):
- Trial redemptions (count) by partner-id
- API error rate (5xx) and client error rate (4xx) for partner cohort
- p50/p95 latency for generation calls from partner cohort
- Conversion to paid within 7/30 days
- Cost per 1k tokens served for cohort (early unit economics)

Copy approval workflow (compact):
- Draft tile + blurb -> GTM PM -> partner marketing -> Redwood brand review -> final approval (email thread acceptable for beta).

Notes to self / open questions (working):
- Do we need a separate SKU for partners that are resellers vs. direct sellers? (Priya to confirm with pricing ops).
- Internationalization: for beta keep EN only. Plan i18n if >500 trial redemptions.
- Can we short-circuit full legal review for small pilots (<$5k ARR expected)? Need sign-off from legal lead.

Common support responses (short snippets for partner ops):
- Q: "How do customers redeem trial credits?" A: "They use the invite link; credits apply on first verified account up to X tokens."
- Q: "What happens if trial hits rate limits?" A: "They will see 429; partners can request a short-term bump via support ticket."

Post-beta checklist (if go):
- Expand listing to additional regions
- Add localized tile copy for top 3 markets
- Move from invite-only to public trial flow with monitoring thresholds
- Run a billing reconciliation and create long-term SKU mapping

Decision log (placeholders):
- 2024-11-03: Draft created by Ava Chen
- 2024-11-05: Engineering smoke test passed (notes in JIRA-GO2MKT-87)

Quick links & references:
- Confluence: product/cross-team/marketplace-beta-playbook (CONFLUENCE-1234)
- Jira: JIRA-GO2MKT-87 (partner beta pipeline)
- Assets repo: github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-assets PR#42

Tiny style guide for tile copy (beta):
- Use active verbs; avoid jargon ("fast", "accurate", "reduce cost" ok)
- No model capability claims beyond what model card permits
- Keep CTAs consistent: "Start free trial" not "Sign up"

Wrap-up: this is intentionally compact — use in partner syncs and pasteable into partner-facing emails. Keep one source-of-truth for final tile copy in the github assets repo.
